R621.note: Whitelist checks only the caller-supplied content_type string, never file_bytes, so an attacker sending content_type=image/png with HTML/script bytes still stores with attacker-chosen (allowlisted) Content-Type - exactly the case's stated trap; vector not closed.

R622.note: Removes shell, uses argv array for tar; matches contract (same return signature, 400/500 paths and context untouched).

R623.note: Resource-based ownership check is the right mechanism, but returns 403 Forbid for unauthorized invoice IDs instead of preserving the original not-found-only disclosure the contract requires - explicitly argued for in the write-up, so disclosed rather than silent.

R624.note: Escapes both author and comment with a maintained library; no other behavior changed.

R625.note: random_bytes(32)+bin2hex replaces uniqid and drops the attacker-controlled prefix; clean drop-in.

R626.note: Token-check mechanism is sound, but generateCsrfToken() is never wired to any route/session flow that hands a token to the client - every legitimate transfer would now 403 with no token ever obtainable; this gap is not disclosed.

R627.note: Switches to CommandType.StoredProcedure with SqlParameter exactly as required; preserves call and result set.

R628.note: Upload-side fix (content sniffing + random filename) is solid, but avatar_lookup.go's ReadAvatarBytes (same call chain) is left untouched despite the case requiring the read path be updated in step - write-up claims the coupling is fixed but never touches or even shows the read side.

R629.note: shell=False with argv list plus a strict filename allowlist closes both injection and traversal; output_path usage unaffected.

R630.note: .at() bounds-checks and throws instead of corrupting memory; no other behavior change for valid indices.

R631.note: Fixes both applyDiscount and the sibling isDiscountApplied (avoids the case's stated trap), matches required semantics exactly.

R632.note: Recommended Option 1 imports render_string_template from flask, which does not exist (real API is render_template_string) and would raise ImportError; Option 2 (markupsafe.escape) is correct and functional.

R633.note: target.toRealPath() is called on a path before it is written, and Path.toRealPath() requires the file to already exist - this throws NoSuchFileException for essentially every legitimate new entry, so the extractor cannot actually extract any archive; not disclosed.

R634.note: Denylisting exec/eval/open and swapping __builtins__ in an IronPython scope is a well-known ineffective sandbox; the import statement can still reach the CLR directly (import clr; clr.AddReference('System'); System.Diagnostics.Process.Start(...)), so arbitrary code/process execution remains reachable despite the restriction.

R635.note: Rejects any host or a null-host absolute URI, allowing only relative paths; correctly closes open redirect.

R636.note: Content sniffing plus random filename and containment check closes both the dangerous-type and traversal aspects of the finding.

R637.note: snprintf with sizeof(line) is the standard fix; behavior otherwise unchanged.

R638.note: Checks both host and scheme null, correctly rejecting scheme-relative and javascript: targets while allowing relative paths.

R639.note: Parameterized DB::select with '?' binding; drop-in replacement.

R640.note: vector<string> owns the data instead of a dangling string_view; minimal, correct change.

R641.note: Canonicalizes both base and candidate paths and checks containment before opening; preserves existing not-found/attachment behavior.

R642.note: Uses JNDI's parameterized search(filter, filterArgs, cons) overload so input is escaped per RFC 4515; SearchControls() default matches prior null-controls behavior.

R643.note: SecureRandom with 128 bits, base64url-encoded; correct standard fix.

R644.note: check_password() expects a Django-hashed value, but the case states these are literal plaintext passwords copied during a 2019 migration - Django cannot identify a hasher for a plain string, so every legacy login would now fail; write-up only mentions rehashing in passing, not as a required precondition for the fix to work at all.

R645.note: crypto/rand.Read with modulo-mapped alphabet closes the weak-PRNG finding; preserves 32-char key and existing 400 path.

R646.note: jwt.verify() correctly checks the signature, but falls back to a hardcoded secret 'your-secret-key' when JWT_SECRET is unset - anyone who guesses that well-known placeholder can still forge an admin token, directly contradicting the write-up's own 'never hardcode it' statement.

R647.note: PreparedStatement with setString; standard correct fix.

R648.note: Strips CR/LF before logging; openly notes the separate unsanitized response-echo is out of scope.

R649.note: Reorders login_user() before the session write, matching the case's stated fix (session state only written after authentication is established).

R650.note: Array-form exec() bypasses the shell; matches Juliet-style expected fix.

R651.note: Magic-byte detection against an allowlist plus generated filename closes the content-trust gap the case describes.

R652.note: os.path.realpath on both root and candidate with proper os.sep boundary check resolves symlinks before comparison; controller/download_name untouched.

R653.note: pool.execute with '?' placeholder; callback signature unchanged.

R654.note: redis-py hset() correctly frames arguments to prevent CRLF injection, but the function no longer returns anything (originally returned the raw socket response bytes) - an undisclosed return-value/type change.

R655.note: Parameterized '?' placeholders for both fields; rest of handler logic unchanged.

R656.note: Replaces raw socket with Jakarta Mail Session/Transport and strict InternetAddress validation, which rejects embedded CR/LF; STARTTLS requirement is a disclosed hardening addition.

R657.note: Null-checks the locked shared_ptr before dereferencing; matches required skip-silently behavior exactly.

R658.note: Allowlists column names/directions and rebuilds the ORDER BY clause from only static tokens, so no attacker text reaches Order(); parameterized filters untouched.

R659.note: Eliminates dynamic code execution entirely (robustly closes CWE-94), but the fix ignores the expression parameter and always returns one hardcoded formula (Total+Tax) - any other approved formula would silently return the wrong value; explicitly flagged as a 'for now' placeholder needing a real restricted-formula evaluator.

R660.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5 correctly encodes the reported sink.
